extracted.intended_audience: agency staff, administrative law attorneys, license applicants, and regulated parties in Florida (practitioners using Chapter 120 procedures)
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory procedural rules from Florida's Administrative Procedure Act (Ch. 120) governing protests, mediation, summary hearings, attorney's fees, licensing, investigations, exemptions, administrative law judges, and ex parte communications in administrative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver for failure to file formal written protest
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file a formal written protest shall constitute a waiver of proceedings under this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The formal written protest must be timely filed; if not filed, the right to proceed is waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirement for formal written protest
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal written protest shall state with particularity the facts and law upon which the protest is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests must set out specific factual and legal grounds — general or vague statements are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of 72-hour time periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Saturdays, Sundays, and state holidays shall be excluded in the computation of the 72-hour time periods provided by this paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines tied to 72-hour rules do not count weekends or state holidays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency stay upon timely-filed protest
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of the formal written protest that has been timely filed, the agency shall stop the solicitation or contract award process until the subject of the protest is resolved by final agency action, unless the agency head sets forth in writing particular facts and circumstances which require continuance to avoid immediate and serious danger to public health, safety, or welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency head may continue process only by written finding showing immediate and serious danger to public interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to resolve protest by mutual agreement (7-day toll)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall provide an opportunity to resolve the protest by mutual agreement between the parties within 7 days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and state holidays, after receipt of a formal written protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties have an initial 7-day period (weekends/holidays excluded) to attempt settlement before further procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal proceeding when no disputed material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the subject of a protest is not resolved by mutual agreement within 7 days and if there is no disputed issue of material fact, an informal proceeding shall be conducted pursuant to subsection (2) and applicable agency rules before a person whose qualifications have been prescribed by rules of the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When facts are undisputed, an informal, non-adversarial proceeding may resolve the protest under agency rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to division when disputed material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the protest is not resolved by mutual agreement within 7 days and there is a disputed issue of material fact, the agency shall refer the protest to the division by electronic means through the division’s website for proceedings under subsection (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disputed factual issues trigger formal referral to the Division of Administrative Hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director must expedite hearing and ALJ assignment timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a formal written protest referred to the division, the director shall expedite the hearing and assign an administrative law judge who shall commence a hearing within 30 days after receipt by the division and enter a recommended order within 30 days after the hearing or receipt of the transcript, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compressed timeline: hearing to commence within 30 days of division receipt; recommended order within 30 days after hearing or transcript receipt; parties allowed 10 days to file written exceptions; final agency order entered within 30 days of recommended order, though parties may waive these timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party submissions after bid/proposal opening not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: In a protest to an invitation to bid or request for proposals procurement, no submissions made after the bid or proposal opening which amend or supplement the bid or proposal shall be considered. For invitation to negotiate procurement, no submissions made after the agency announces its intent to award, reject all replies, or withdraw the solicitation which amend or supplement the reply shall be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-opening amendments/supplements are excluded from consideration in procurement protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on protesting party
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided by statute, the burden of proof shall rest with the party protesting the proposed agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protester must prove the agency action is improper under applicable standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: De novo proceedings for competitive-procurement protests
rubrics_metrics.description: In a competitive-procurement protest, other than a rejection of all bids, proposals, or replies, the administrative law judge shall conduct a de novo proceeding to determine whether the agency’s proposed action is contrary to the agency’s governing statutes, rules or policies, or solicitation specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALJ reviews the matter anew (de novo) examining compliance with statutes, rules, policies, and specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof for competitive-procurement protests
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard of proof for such proceedings shall be whether the proposed agency action was clearly erroneous, contrary to competition, arbitrary, or capricious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALJ evaluates whether agency action meets these judicially recognized standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of review for protests contesting rejection of all bids
rubrics_metrics.description: In any bid-protest proceeding contesting an intended agency action to reject all bids, proposals, or replies, the standard of review by an administrative law judge shall be whether the agency’s intended action is illegal, arbitrary, dishonest, or fraudulent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher threshold: allegations must show illegality, arbitrariness, dishonesty, or fraud to overturn a rejection of all bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal disposition permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless precluded by law, informal disposition may be made of any proceeding by stipulation, agreed settlement, or consent order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may settle or stipulate to resolve matters without formal adjudication unless statute prohibits it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediation notice requirement in announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each announcement of an agency action that affects substantial interests shall advise whether mediation of the administrative dispute for the type of agency action announced is available and that choosing mediation does not affect the right to an administrative hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notices must inform parties about mediation availability and preservation of hearing rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolling of time limits for mediation agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency and all parties agree to mediation in writing within 10 days after the time period stated in the announcement for election of an administrative remedy, the time limitations imposed by ss. 120.569 and 120.57 shall be tolled to allow mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written agreement to mediate within the 10-day window pauses statutory deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediation duration and required agreement provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The mediation shall be concluded within 60 days of such agreement unless otherwise agreed. The mediation agreement shall include provisions for mediator selection, the allocation of costs and fees associated with mediation, and the mediating parties’ understanding regarding the confidentiality of discussions and documents introduced during mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mediation agreements must address mediator selection, cost allocation, and confidentiality; parties may extend timelines by agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of mediation settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: If mediation results in settlement of the administrative dispute, the agency shall enter a final order incorporating the agreement of the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlements reached in mediation should be memorialized in final agency orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary hearing initial order timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 5 business days following the division’s receipt of a petition or request for hearing, the division shall issue and serve on all original parties an initial order assigning the case to a specific ALJ and providing general information regarding practice and procedure; the initial order shall state that a summary hearing is available and briefly describe expedited time sequences, limited discovery, and final order provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early notice to parties about assignment and summary hearing option is mandatory within 5 business days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and consent for summary hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 15 days after service of the initial order, any party may file a motion for summary hearing. If all original parties agree in writing, the summary proceeding shall be conducted within 30 days of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary hearing requires motion within 15 days and unanimous written consent to be expedited within 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervenors bound by original parties' decision on summary hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervenors shall be governed by the decision of the original parties regarding whether the case will proceed as a summary hearing and shall not have standing to challenge that decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervenors cannot override unanimous choice of original parties for summary procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of permissible motions in summary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions shall be limited to: (1) a motion in opposition to the petition; (2) a motion requesting discovery beyond informal exchange (additional discovery may be permitted upon a showing of necessity but must be completable not later than 5 days prior to final hearing); (3) a motion for continuance of the final hearing; (4) a motion requesting a prehearing conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery is restricted; additional discovery only for necessity and must fit tight deadlines; prehearing conferences can be required or requested to narrow issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing conference purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: A prehearing conference is for identifying legal/factual issues, names/addresses of witnesses, documentary evidence to be offered, the range of penalties that may be imposed, and any other matter the ALJ determines would expedite resolution; it may be held by telephone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prehearing conference is focused on case management and narrowing scope for summary disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document exchange deadline for summary hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Not later than 5 days prior to the final hearing, the parties shall furnish to each other copies of documentary evidence and lists of witnesses who may testify at the final hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict 5-day pre-hearing exchange requirement for documents and witness lists in summary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic procedural rights in summary hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties shall have an opportunity to respond, present evidence and argument on all issues involved, conduct cross-examination, submit rebuttal evidence, and be represented by counsel or other qualified representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in expedited summary hearings, core due-process rights (presentation, cross-examination, counsel) are preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited record in summary cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The record shall consist only of: notices, pleadings, motions, intermediate rulings, evidence received, matters officially recognized, proffers of proof and objections and rulings thereon, matters placed on the record after ex parte communication, the written decision of the ALJ, and the official transcript of the final hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record is narrowly defined for summary hearings and thus limits what the ALJ may base findings on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of testimony and transcript availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall accurately and completely preserve all testimony in the proceeding and, upon request by any party, shall make a full or partial transcript available at no more than actual cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure record preservation and permit parties access to transcripts at cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ decision timing and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision of the ALJ shall be rendered within 30 days after the conclusion of the final hearing or filing of the transcript, whichever is later. The decision shall include findings of fact based exclusively on the evidence of record and matters officially recognized, conclusions of law, imposition of any fines or penalties if applicable, and any other information required by law or rule to be contained in a final order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALJ decisions in summary matters are time-limited (30 days) and must explicitly state factual findings tied to the record and legal conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney’s fees awarded only for improper purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The final order in a proceeding pursuant to s. 120.57(1) shall award reasonable costs and a reasonable attorney’s fee to the prevailing party only where the nonprevailing adverse party has been determined by the ALJ to have participated in the proceeding for an improper purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are not automatic to prevailing parties; they require a finding of improper purpose by the nonprevailing adverse party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and factors for 'improper purpose'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Improper purpose' means participation primarily to harass, to cause unnecessary delay, for frivolous purpose, or to needlessly increase the cost of litigation, licensing, or securing approval of an activity. The ALJ shall consider whether the nonprevailing adverse party participated in two or more other proceedings involving the same prevailing party and same project without establishing merits, creating a rebuttable presumption of improper purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pattern litigation against the same party/project can create a presumption of improper purpose; findings are based on history and merits of positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of 'costs' and 'nonprevailing adverse party' for fee awards
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Costs' has the same meaning as costs allowed in civil actions in Florida (chapter 57). 'Nonprevailing adverse party' means a party that has failed to have substantially changed the outcome of the proposed or final agency action which is the subject of a proceeding; parties whose issues result in substantial modification or conditions to resolve matters are not nonprevailing adverse parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination whether a party is 'nonprevailing' depends on whether their action led to substantive changes resolving their concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney’s fees for rule challenges with fee caps
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appellate court or ALJ declares a proposed rule or portion of a proposed rule invalid (s.120.56(2)), or declares an existing rule invalid (s.120.56(3) or (5)), a judgment or order shall be rendered against the agency for reasonable costs and reasonable attorney’s fees unless the agency demonstrates its actions were substantially justified; no award of attorney’s fees under these subsections shall exceed $50,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees against agencies in rule challenges are available but capped at $50,000 unless special circumstances justify otherwise; agencies can avoid fee awards by showing substantial justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies when agency statement violates rule restrictions (s.120.56(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appellate court or ALJ determines that all or part of an agency statement violates s. 120.54(1)(a) or s. 120.56(4)(f), a judgment or order shall be entered against the agency for reasonable costs and reasonable attorney’s fees unless the agency demonstrates the statement is required by the federal government to implement/retain a delegated program or to meet a condition to receipt of federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency reliance on an unadopted rule can result in fee awards unless federally required; additional procedural safeguards (notice, stays) may apply and awards may be capped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment source for certain fee awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding chapter 284, an award under s.120.56(4) shall be paid from the budget entity of the secretary, executive director, or equivalent administrative officer of the agency; the agency shall not be entitled to payment of an award or reimbursement for payment of an award under any provision of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards in these contexts are charged to the agency head's budget entity and are not reimbursable elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals fee awards for frivolous appeals or gross abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is an appeal, the court in its discretion may award reasonable attorney’s fees and costs to the prevailing party if it finds the appeal was frivolous, meritless, an abuse of the appellate process, or that the agency action which precipitated the appeal was a gross abuse of discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may sanction frivolous appeals or agency gross abuse with fee awards covering administrative and appellate proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency examination of license application within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a license application, an agency shall examine the application and, within 30 days after such receipt, notify the applicant of any apparent errors or omissions and request any additional information the agency is permitted by law to require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely agency review and prompt notification of defects are mandatory; failure to timely notify prevents denial for errors/omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency cannot deny for failure to correct unless timely notified
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may not deny a license for failure to correct an error or omission or to supply additional information unless the agency timely notified the applicant within this 30-day period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants protected from denial if agency did not timely identify deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and 90-day decision requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is complete upon receipt of all requested information; a license application must be approved or denied within 90 days after receipt of a completed application unless a shorter period is provided by law. The 90-day time period is tolled by initiation of a proceeding under ss. 120.569 and 120.57.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default 90-day decision window applies to completed applications; tolling occurs if adjudicatory proceedings begin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed approval (default license) mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application not approved or denied within the 90-day or shorter time period, within 15 days after conclusion of a public hearing held on the application, or within 45 days after a recommended order is submitted (whichever is latest), is considered approved unless the recommended order recommends denial. An applicant seeking to claim licensure by default must notify the agency clerk in writing of intent and may not act on the default license until receipt of such notice by the clerk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow formal notice procedures to claim a default/ deemed-approved license; certain conditions (e.g., pending recommended order) can prevent default approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency notice of licensing actions must state grounds with particularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant shall be given written notice that the agency intends to grant or deny, or has granted or denied, the application. The notice must state with particularity the grounds or basis for the issuance or denial of the license, except when issuance is a ministerial act, and must inform recipients of available administrative hearing or judicial review, applicable procedures, and time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed written grounds and instructions about remedies and timelines are mandatory in licensing notices; copies must be provided to attorneys of record and requestors for notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal applications preserve existing license during processing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a licensee has made timely and sufficient application for renewal (for licenses that do not automatically expire by statute), the existing license shall not expire until the application has been finally acted on, or until the last day for seeking review of the agency order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees retain licensure while a timely renewal application is pending and until appeal periods lapse if denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements before revocation/suspension: notice and opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: No revocation, suspension, annulment, or withdrawal of any license is lawful unless, prior to the entry of a final order, the agency has served, by personal service or certified mail, an administrative complaint which affords reasonable notice to the licensee of facts or conduct which warrant the intended action and unless the licensee has been given an adequate opportunity to request a proceeding under ss. 120.569 and 120.57.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due process requires personal or certified mail service of complaints and opportunity for adjudicatory proceedings before depriving a licensee of license rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication remedy when certified mail notice returns undelivered
rubrics_metrics.description: When personal service cannot be made and the certified mail notice is returned undelivered, the agency shall cause a short, plain notice to the licensee to be published once each week for 4 consecutive weeks in a newspaper published in the county of the licensee’s last known address; if no newspaper is published there, a general-circulation county newspaper may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in local newspapers is an alternate notice method where certified mail fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency suspension procedural safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency finds immediate serious danger to public health, safety, or welfare requires emergency suspension, restriction, or limitation of a license, the agency may take such action by any procedure that is fair under the circumstances, provided: (a) the procedure provides at least the same procedural protection as other statutes/constitutions; (b) agency takes only necessary action to protect public interest; and (c) the agency states in writing specific facts and reasons for finding immediate danger and concluding the procedure used is fair. These findings are judicially reviewable, and a suspension proceeding under ss. 120.569 and 120.57 shall also be promptly instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency actions are allowed but must be narrowly tailored, documented in writing, provide procedural fairness, and be subject to prompt follow-up proceedings and judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions based on other agency statements require legal authority and opportunity to challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: No agency shall include as a condition of approval of any license any provision that is based upon a statement, policy, or guideline of another agency unless the other agency identifies specific legal authority for each such statement, policy, or guideline. The licensing agency must provide the licensee an opportunity to challenge the condition as invalid and may require the other agency to join as a party in determining validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions relying on another agency's policies must be legally grounded and subject to challenge, with the other agency potentially joined to defend the condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to transcript/recording and counsel in agency investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person who responds to a request or demand by any agency for written data or an oral statement is entitled to a transcript or recording of his or her oral statement at no more than cost. Any person compelled or appearing before any presiding officer or agency in an investigation or proceeding has the right, at his or her own expense, to be accompanied, represented, and advised by counsel or other qualified representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents may obtain records of their statements and have legal representation (at their expense) in investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration Commission exemption criteria and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon application of any agency, the Administration Commission may exempt any process or proceeding governed by this act from one or more requirements when: (a) the agency head certifies conflict with federal law or rules; (b) to permit receipt of tax benefits or federal funds; or (c) conformity would be so inconvenient or impractical as to defeat the agency proceeding or purpose and would not be in the public interest. The commission must establish alternative procedures consistent with intent and hold a public hearing with notice; it must issue an order granting/denying the exemption and prescribe alternative procedures. Exemptions terminate 90 days following adjournment sine die of the then-current or next legislative session or upon effective date of subsequent legislation; renewals permitted once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions are narrowly circumscribed, require public process, alternative procedures, and have built-in expiration and limited renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ qualifications and division structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Administrative Hearings shall be headed by a director appointed by the Administration Commission; any person employed as an administrative law judge must have been a member of The Florida Bar in good standing for the preceding 5 years. The division is a separate budget entity, and the director serves as agency head; Department of Management Services provides support but not control over the division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ALJs must be experienced Florida Bar members and the division operates with institutional independence and specified governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's and division authorities and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The director has the right to appeal certain Executive Office of the Governor actions affecting the division's budget or personnel to the Administration Commission. The division shall employ ALJs, may provide ALJs on contract to other governmental entities, and shall issue an annual written report to specified committees including summaries of utilization, recommendations, and compliance reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Division leadership has specified administrative authorities and reporting obligations to ensure accountability and resource management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of specialized ALJs for health-related cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division shall designate at least two administrative law judges to preside over actions involving the Department of Health or boards within it; each designated ALJ must be a Florida Bar member in good standing and have legal, managerial, or clinical experience in health care issues or board certification in health care law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Health-related disputes should be handled by ALJs with specialized health-care-related credentials or experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement and withholding for ALJ services (school boards)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a district school board fails to make a timely payment for services provided by an ALJ, the Commissioner of Education shall withhold from general revenue funds an amount sufficient to pay for the ALJ’s services and transfer the amount to the Division of Administrative Hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism exists to enforce payment for ALJ services by withholding state funds from nonpaying school districts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on ex parte communications after recommended order
rubrics_metrics.description: In any proceeding under ss. 120.569 and 120.57, no ex parte communication relative to the merits, threat, or offer of reward shall be made to the agency head after the agency head has received a recommended order, or to the presiding officer by (a) agency personnel engaged in prosecution/advocacy, or (b) a party or the party’s representative or any person who would have a substantial interest in the proposed agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict ban on ex parte contacts affecting merits after a recommended order is received; exceptions exclude advisory staff who do not testify and rulemaking proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer duties upon receiving prohibited ex parte communication
rubrics_metrics.description: A presiding officer who receives an ex parte communication in violation must place on the record all written communications received, written responses, and a memorandum stating the substance of oral communications and responses, and must advise all parties that such matters have been placed on the record. Any party may request opportunity to rebut within 10 days after notice. The presiding officer may withdraw and be replaced to eliminate effect of ex parte communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory disclosure and opportunity to rebut are required to mitigate effects of prohibited ex parte contacts; recusal is permitted if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for prohibited ex parte communications and failure to record
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who makes a prohibited ex parte communication, and any presiding officer who fails to place such communication in the record, is in violation and may be assessed a civil penalty not to exceed $500 or be subjected to other disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement includes civil penalties (up to $500) and disciplinary measures for violators and non-disclosing presiding officers.
